title: Silicon and light: electricity without a reaction

concepts.label: covalent bond (shared electron pair)
concepts.definition: A bond made of two electrons, one from each of two neighbouring atoms, that both atoms count toward their full shell; silicon makes four, so no ions form.

concepts.label: semiconductor
concepts.definition: A covalent crystal (silicon, germanium, GaAs, CdTe) whose valence electrons are all in bonds but can be freed by a modest push from heat, light or foreign atoms, so its conductivity can be set over many powers of ten.

concepts.label: electron-volt (eV)
concepts.definition: The energy one electron gains when pushed through one volt: 1 eV = 1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, or 96.5 kJ per mole of electrons.

concepts.label: band gap
concepts.definition: The energy needed to free one bonded electron inside the crystal (silicon 1.12 eV, germanium 0.67, GaAs 1.42, CdTe 1.5, diamond 5.47); an electron given less falls back.

concepts.label: hole
concepts.definition: A bond with one electron missing; it behaves as a mobile +1 charge because neighbouring bond electrons hop into it, and it vanishes when a free electron recombines with it.

concepts.label: doping: n-type (extra electrons)
concepts.definition: Silicon with a few group-15 atoms (phosphorus) swapped in: each gives one free electron and stays behind as a fixed P⁺ ion, so the mobile carriers are negative.

concepts.label: doping: p-type (holes)
concepts.definition: Silicon with a few group-13 atoms (boron) swapped in: each takes one bond electron, becoming a fixed B⁻ ion and releasing a mobile hole, so the mobile carriers are positive.

concepts.label: p–n junction
concepts.definition: The boundary between p-type and n-type regions of one crystal, where electrons and holes have recombined and left a thin carrier-free layer of bare fixed ions.

concepts.label: built-in field
concepts.definition: The electric field across a p–n junction, set up by the bare P⁺ ions on the n side and B⁻ ions on the p side; it pushes electrons to the n side and holes to the p side (about 0.7 V in silicon).

concepts.label: photon (energy by colour)
concepts.definition: A packet of light whose energy is fixed by its wavelength: E (eV) ≈ 1240 / wavelength (nm); red about 1.8 eV, violet about 3.1 eV.

concepts.label: photovoltaic effect
concepts.definition: A photon with at least the band-gap energy frees an electron–hole pair, the junction's field separates them, and the electron returns to the hole through the external circuit: light becomes current with no chemical change.

concepts.label: below-gap and heat losses
concepts.definition: Photons below the gap pass through unused and the energy of a photon above the gap is lost as heat, which caps a single-junction cell near 44% from these two losses alone and about 33% in full (Shockley–Queisser limit).

concepts.label: I–V curve
concepts.definition: The set of current–voltage pairs a lit cell can deliver, from the short-circuit current at 0 V (9 A for the running cell) to the open-circuit voltage at 0 A (about 0.64 V for silicon).

concepts.label: maximum power point
concepts.definition: The point on the I–V curve where the product V × I is largest (about 0.56 V × 8.6 A ≈ 4.8 W for the running cell); the load must be matched to it.

namedOnly: valence band / conduction band (named once as the physicists' terms for 'held in a bond' / 'free to roam')
recombination (electron drops back into a hole; used as plain vocabulary from step 4)
insulator (glass, diamond: bond electrons too tightly held)
depletion layer (described as the carrier-free strip of bare ions, not named)
resistance / ohm (used as 'volts needed per ampere'; pointer to Real batteries)
gallium arsenide and cadmium telluride (group 13+15 and 12+16 crystals averaging four valence electrons)
cells in a chain (series) adding voltages in a panel; maximum-power-point tracking electronics
thermal energy about 0.026 eV at room temperature (stated as a typical jostle)
summary: Running example: one 156 mm silicon cell (243 cm², about 10 g) in full sun, 24.3 W of light in, 9 A short-circuit, 0.64 V open-circuit, about 4.8 W at the maximum power point; built up from one silicon atom sharing four electron pairs, through the 1.12 eV band gap, holes, phosphorus/boron doping and the p–n junction, to photons freeing pairs. It is contrasted with the Daniell cell's 6.54 g zinc strip (5.36 Ah stored, reactant consumed) to make the point that a solar cell stores nothing and converts. Capstone: a simulator with light intensity, band gap (Ge/Si/GaAs/CdTe presets) and load resistance, an animated cell cross-section, a traceable I–V curve with maximum power point and an energy-budget bar chart. Hooks: the electron-volt (1 eV per electron = 96.5 kJ/mol), 'power = area of the V × I rectangle', load matching, and band gap as a material property set by the elements chosen.
